dataset: CDC BRFSS employed-adult finite-file replay frames, 2023 and 2024

year.definition: BRFSS survey year; these are independent cross-sections, not linked respondents

state.definition: Two-character _STATE FIPS code; read as string to preserve leading zero. Primary frame contains 47 common states and DC

state_name.definition: Name transcribed programmatically from the corresponding CDC codebook

health.definition: (30 - mental_unhealthy_days)/3; higher means fewer self-reported mentally unhealthy days. This is an analysis rescaling, not the NHS burnout score

weight.definition: Original combined landline/cellphone final survey weight as represented in the ASCII public file. Retained for explicit sensitivity analyses; not used to define the primary unweighted respondent-file target

stratum.definition: Published survey-design stratum; scope jointly with year and state

psu.definition: Published survey-design primary-sampling-unit code, not a name/contact identifier; scope jointly with year and state

anonymrow.definition: First 24 hexadecimal characters of SHA256(year:ASCII_zip_sha256:physical_record_ordinal). Stable within this exact public release, not a longitudinal person ID

mental_unhealthy_days.definition: Core past-30-day mentally unhealthy-day response. Code 88 becomes zero; codes 77, 99 and blank are excluded. Codes 1–30 are retained

frequent_mental_distress.definition: 1 if mental_unhealthy_days is at least 14, otherwise 0; derived from the core answer rather than overriding it from _MENT14D

employment_code.definition: 1 employed for wages; 2 self-employed. Other categories, refused and missing employment are outside this frame

employment_category.definition: Employment status, not industry or occupation

is_state_or_dc.definition: 1 for state/DC public codes through 56; 0 for the three territories. Always 1 in primary common-group CSVs; useful in all_areas CSVs

reference_scope: Complete-file oracle summaries for evaluation and documented 2023-only calibration. 2024 complete-frame outcomes, means and variances must not be supplied to an acquisition policy
finite_file_variance: Population variance with denominator N over the retained respondent records, not a survey-population variance or an unbiased sample-variance estimate
finite_file_weighted_ratio: Sum(weight * health)/sum(weight) over all retained records. This is a second finite-file estimand, not established state-population truth
kish_weight_concentration_n: (sum weights)^2/sum(weights^2). Describes weight concentration only; excludes clustering, stratification, outcome dependence, nonresponse and other design effects. Do not label it a complete survey effective sample size
industry: Not included. Industry/occupation modules do not have uniform national coverage and may require questionnaire-version-specific weights. No employer, hospital or department is inferred
